svg.text: claudia — While working: “Arial, shown as Liberation Sans”, proposed
The stand-in stays visible for as long as it is used: in the header bar, on the text itself if asked, and wherever a font is chosen. creates shown; the same in composes and computes.
A · The presentation, with its stand-ins in view
One quiet chip in the header bar while any stand-in is in use; its popover names each pair.
Title · Arial, shown as Liberation Sans (same widths)
Mark text set in a stand-in
B · Choosing a font: the name, and what shows it
Edit This Style… and the style popover use the same field.
Arial is not here. Laid out, shown and printed with Liberation Sans, which
has the same widths. Exports write Arial.
shown as Liberation Sans · same widths
In the header bar, next to the connection indicator, only while a
stand-in is in use. It says how many; the words are the same as on
import: stand-in, same widths, other widths.
Each pair as "Arial → Liberation Sans". Mark text set in a stand-in is
View ▸ Show Stand-in Fonts (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+B, free in all three): a
Hovering text, a selection or an object tells its style and font in one
line. Screen readers get the same sentence from the style field.
Where the stand-in breaks lines differently, text that no longer fits
its box shows the overflow mark; these are the slides the import
The field shows the name the style asks for, in the stand-in's face,
then "shown as …". Picking Liberation Sans on purpose is a different
thing: the style then asks for Liberation Sans, and exports write that.
Names with a stand-in get a second line, so choosing Arial never
hides that Liberation Sans will draw it.
